Burnham to announce plans for new North Sea oil and gas drilling.
- Andy Burnham will announce plans for new oil and gas drilling in the North Sea when he becomes PM on Monday, the BBC has been told.
- Labour's 2024 manifesto (which Burnham said he would follow) pledged not to issue new licences but to honour existing ones.
- At heart of debate: two Scottish oil/gas fields, Rosebank and Jackdaw, approved 2022/2023 under Conservatives, overturned in 2025 after legal challenge; public consultations launched (close August).
- Announcement part of a "flurry" of measures: water and energy under public control, new council house-building programme.
- A source close to Burnham: no final decisions in this area yet made; plans likely unveiled at a later date, not day one.
- Earlier in week, oil & gas industry and trade unions wrote to Labour MPs urging them to "back North Sea oil and gas": support is "a signal that the country remains committed to producing, building and manufacturing... that government backs the people and places that have powered this country for generations."
